mechanism_narrative: A higher level of the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) indicates elevated inflation, which increases the perceived risk of holding equities and reduces the real value of future cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for CPIAUCSL as a predictor of 20-day returns remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or the correlation between CPIAUCSL and 20-day returns is positive in more than 40% of 20-day windows.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeds 6.0% for three consecutive months, it signals a deteriorating labor market, which is a leading indicator of economic contraction and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for UNRATE > 6.0% for 3 months as a trigger for negative returns is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 5-day returns in triggered periods are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) signals an imminent recession, which increases the risk of equity holdings and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO and PAYEMS both decline from prior month
failure_condition: The Rank IC for the joint condition (INDPRO and PAYEMS decline) as a trigger for negative returns is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 60-day returns in triggered periods are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When residential fixed investment (RSAFS) falls below its 1-year moving average, it indicates a contraction in the housing sector, which is a leading indicator of economic weakness and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for RSAFS < 1-year moving average as a trigger for negative returns is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day returns in triggered periods are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 1.0% signals the Federal Reserve's commitment to monetary easing, which reduces the risk-free rate and increases the present value of equity cash flows, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for FEDFUNDS < 1.0% as a trigger for positive returns is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 5-day returns in triggered periods are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A higher unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a deteriorating labor market, which increases the perceived risk of economic contraction and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for UNRATE as a predictor of 60-day returns remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or the correlation between UNRATE and 60-day returns is positive in more than 40% of 60-day windows.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and rise in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) signals stagflation, which increases the risk of equity holdings and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines and CPIAUCSL rises from prior month
failure_condition: The Rank IC for the joint condition (INDPRO decline and CPIAUCSL rise) as a trigger for negative returns is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day returns in triggered periods are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In a recession regime (defined by INDPRO < 100), the decline in industrial production signals economic contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The Rank IC for INDPRO < 100 as a trigger for negative returns is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 60-day returns in triggered periods are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).
